chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha', from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

We are patient, and our Shia are more patient than us. I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, how did your Shia become more patient than you?' He said, 'Because we are patient upon what we know, and our Shia are patient upon what they do not know.'

key_terms.صُبُرٌ: patient (plural of sabr, indicating a high degree of patience)
key_terms.عَلَى مَا لَا يَعْلَمُونَ: upon what they do not know

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the patience of the Imams and the patience of the Shia according to Hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the spiritual status of the Shia by contrasting their patience in the unknown (ghayb) with the Imams' patience in the known. This distinction highlights the unique trial of the faithful who must maintain steadfastness without the direct guidance or immediate certainty possessed by the Imams, a concept deeply rooted in Shia eschatology and the era of the Minor and Major Occultation. The narration underscores that true devotion is proven not just by enduring what is understood, but by persevering through ambiguity and hidden divine decrees.
